---
title: Contributing to the catalog
description: Add a provider Teire can read, or a change it missed, through a pull request. CI checks it against the same schema Teire uses, and a merged record is live on the next deploy.
icon: GitPullRequestArrow
---

Most of Teire's catalog is generated: diffs of package versions, advisories, and the pages of the providers your code talks to, read with their quotes checked. Two kinds of record live in the repository instead, under `catalog/`, so anyone can add or correct them, a provider's own team included.

## A provider Teire can read

`catalog/providers/<slug>.json` describes a provider: its name, its official domains (quotes count only from those), its SDKs, how a repository shows it uses it, and the pages Teire reads. A deprecation page that publishes one table row per retired model or endpoint needs no code: the generic table reader takes its layout from the record.

```json title="catalog/providers/openai.json (the source)"
{
  "kind": "deprecations",
  "url": "https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md",
  "adapter": "deprecation-table",
  "table": { "sectionLevel": 3 }
}
```

| Key | What it says |
|---|---|
| `sectionLevel` | The heading level that starts each dated announcement (`###` is 3); 0 when the page is one table |
| `subjectColumn` | The header of what goes away (a pattern; default: a "model", "snapshot" or "system" column) |
| `dateColumn` | The header of when (default: "shutdown", "retirement" or "removal") |
| `replacementColumn` | The header of what replaces it (default: "replacement" or "substitute") |
| `skipSection` | Section headings to leave out |

## A change Teire missed

`catalog/changes/<subject>/<id>.json` is one change record in Teire's contract (`catalog/schema/change-v2.schema.json`): `<subject>` is the provider's slug or the package's name, and the id starts with `contrib-`, so it can never be one of Teire's generated records. A contributed record says it was contributed, who added it and in which pull request:

```json title="provenance"
{
  "method": "catalog",
  "contributor": {
    "login": "your-github-login",
    "pullRequest": "https://github.com/teire-dev/teire/pull/123"
  },
  "confidence": { "overall": 1 }
}
```

Every source keeps its quote and the page it came from, as Teire's own records do, and the record is public.

## What CI checks

`pnpm --filter @teire/engine catalog:validate` runs on every pull request:

- each provider and change file against the schema;
- a provider file named after its slug;
- a contributed change marked `"method": "catalog"`, public, in its subject's folder, with a `contrib-` id no other record uses;
- for each record the pull request adds or changes: the contributor is the pull request's author and names this pull request, and every source passes the gate Teire's own records pass: on the provider's own domains, fetched by CI, with its quote really on the page;
- `catalog/contributed.json`, the bundle the worker reads, up to date (`catalog:validate --write` rebuilds it).

A record that fails any of these fails the pull request. Once merged, the worker merges every contributed record when it next starts, and its change page shows **added by @login**, linked to the pull request when the record names it.
